new_statements.quote: 4.3.1 Vowel length in the penultimate syllable. This vowel length is conditioned rather than contrastive, and occurs in all multisyllabic words. Phonetically, the vowel can be up to two and a half times as long as a vowel in the anti-penultimate syllable. If the vowel follows a labialised or palatalised consonant, or precedes a prenasalised consonant, there is no additional lengthening of the vowel (see section 4.3.2 for the exception to this). [p. 32-33] ... The tone bearing unit (TBU) in Bungu is analysed as the mora rather than the syllable, and all phonetically long vowels are analysed as consisting of two mora. [p. 40]
new_statements.citation: Gray, Hazel. 2020. Bungu Phonology and Morphophonology. SIL Electronic Working Papers 2020-003. Dallas, Texas: SIL International. 92 pp.
new_statements.locator: §4.3 'Vowel length' and §4.3.1 'Vowel length in the penultimate syllable', pp. 32-33 (PDF pp. 38-39); tone: §6.1 'Generalities', p. 40 (PDF p. 46)
new_statements.rule_in_words: Bungu is described as a tone language (lexical and grammatical tone, mora as TBU); the description never uses the terms 'stress' or 'accent'. The only word-level prominence cue reported is automatic, non-contrastive lengthening of the penultimate syllable of every multisyllabic word (measured at up to 2.5x the antepenult vowel), the usual Bantu penultimate-prominence pattern; lengthening is suppressed after labialised/palatalised consonants and before prenasalised consonants. If this penultimate lengthening is taken as the stress correlate, the reading would be fixed-penult.
new_statements.exceptions: No penultimate lengthening when the penult vowel follows a labialised or palatalised consonant or precedes a prenasalised consonant (p. 32-33, with §4.3.2 exceptions); phrase-final words with a final high tone get boundary-L insertion and final-vowel lengthening instead (§4.3.4, p. 35). Gray also quotes Labroussi (1999:360) that vowel length in Bungu is 'mostly dependent on emphasis and a careful vs. fast articulation', which she rejects for morphological length.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level: 'all multisyllabic words' (verbs and nouns in citation form, measured in recordings of isolated words, Table 22 p. 33); the final-vowel lengthening in §4.3.4 is explicitly phrase-final.
new_statements.identity_note: Gray 2020 describes the Bungu of the villages east of Lake Rukwa (Mwambani, Maleza, Udinde, Manda A consultants; p. 3), i.e. Glottolog bung1265 proper; the survey (Smith et al. 2008) treats the Gua/Manda variety as possibly Kimbu-related, and Gray excludes it. No dialect issue for the stress/length statement.
